phaseCalculation.batteryShares: L1/L2/L3: 100% on selected phase; balanced3: 1/3 per phase; unknown: worst-case full contribution on every phase with no optimistic baseline subtraction
phaseCalculation.baseline: Measured phase net import minus incumbent charging only where distribution is known; include any lost discharge in a command transition.
phaseCalculation.allocation: Preserve safe incumbent allocation, then redistribute only the remaining requested total across eligible batteries within existing SoC/per-battery/total limits.
phaseCalculation.example: 5400 W balanced three-phase charge; L2 5600 W, limit4500 W: total charge limited to2100 W (3300 W reduction).
phaseCalculation.recovery: At most100 W per battery per existing command interval; urgent reduction bypasses ordinary interval; existing pauses/ownership/publication mutex retained.
phaseCalculation.detection: On-demand only, one selected +400 W pulse; two matching fresh responses and two confirmed returns; Split baseline can be100->500->100 W; cancellation/timeout/restart releases existing test ownership and resumes existing EMS scheduling.

autoTune.batterySocReliability: Existing10-minute input-warning freshness threshold; stale SoC excluded from reliable evidence.
autoTune.maximumStep: Low-PV/daily-energy proposals at most1 kWh, normally at most10%; save floor at most2 percentage points.
autoTune.dailyEnergySemantics: Gross non-EV daily household demand; existing planner credits PV once. Desired AutoTune SoC helps assess PV days within actual configured goal, not falsify measured household consumption.
autoTune.energyBalance: Observed uncovered expensive-period demand already deducts concurrent PV once. Nominal battery availability uses maximum applicable technical/seasonal floor, not additive reserves. Future grid charging not counted as already stored energy.
autoTune.confidence: Conservative evidence-count heuristic, not calibrated statistical probability.
